verdict.rationale: The README documents the full install-to-first-task path: plug in the board, which the phone powers; flash it with flash.sh; sign the app with a free Apple ID; complete a four-step setup that checks itself (model endpoint/key, AssistiveTouch pointer calibration); then type a goal and press Start. It is first-party only, the steps are scattered rather than shown as one explicit quickstart, and nothing proves a developer can finish using the docs alone. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on confirmation that a first task completes from the docs alone, a consolidated quickstart page, and detail on app build/install and endpoint provisioning prerequisites.

support.subject: As a developer, I get from install to a first completed device task using the quickstart docs alone

citations.quote: Setup walks through four steps and checks each one itself
Give Me a Brain — enter your model endpoint and key (stored in the Keychain)
Let Me Use the Pointer — turn on AssistiveTouch; the app calibrates the pointer by itself.
Type a goal (for example "Open Settings and go to Wi-Fi") and press Start.
Always build with flash.sh: it applies the BLE buffer sizes in hardware/hid_bridge/nimble_cfg.h.
A free Apple ID can sign it (re-sign every 7 days).
USB-C models plug in directly; Lightning models need a Lightning to USB Camera Adapter. The phone powers the board.
